subject: Playbook — multi-entity invoice distribution and collections cadence
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@elan-ware.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: ElanWare Finance <ap@elan-ware.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Split billing across ELW-US and ELW-EU for Q4 invoice

Hi Stephanie —

Quick note from AP: we have a single consolidated Q4 invoice coming from Redwood but need the invoice split 60/40 between ElanWare US (ELW-US) and ElanWare EU (ELW-EU) for internal chargebacks. The two legal entities also require distinct tax references and the EU portion needs VAT amount broken out.

Can Redwood produce either (a) two separate invoices per legal entity or (b) a single invoice with line-level entity tags that our accounting can ingest? Also need cost-center code mapping for each product line — our internal system will ingest an allocation matrix (we can provide a template).

Attached: ElanWare-entity-mapping-20261129.pdf — shows legal entity ids and VAT numbers.

We need this finalized before Dec 10 to close our books. Any blockers?

Thanks,
Liam
Finance Operations
ElanWare

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Split billing across ELW-US and ELW-EU for Q4 invoice

Forwarding AP ask from ElanWare — they need a repeatable playbook for multi-entity splits and cost center allocations. Their timeline: finalize by Dec 10.

Karthik — can your team produce either separate invoices (per legal entity) or a single invoice with line-level tags? If we need to enable a new invoice pipeline for this customer, what's the operational lead time and any constraints (tax / VAT reporting, cross-entity revenue recognition) we should highlight?

Stephanie Nguyen

Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Split billing across ELW-US and ELW-EU for Q4 invoice

Stephanie —

High level: we support both approaches but with trade-offs. Summary below:

- Two separate invoices (preferred when legal entities require different tax/VAT numbers):
  * Pros: clean legal entity billing, separate tax documents, simpler AR/collections per entity.
  * Cons: adds an extra step in our invoice generator; we need to map each invoice line to an entity at generate-time. Turnaround: ~3 business days once we have the mapping.

- Single invoice with line-level entity tags:
  * Pros: fewer documents to send; simple for customers that prefer consolidated invoices.
  * Cons: requires ElanWare to accept line-level parsing; EU VAT handling still needs a VAT subtotal line for the EU portion. Our accounting ingestion can handle it but some ERPs (older) may not. Turnaround: ~2 business days to enable report/export format.

Operational asks from our side:
1) Allocation matrix (product line -> entity -> cost_center_code). See attached template we usually send.
2) Confirmation of which discounts/credits apply to which entity.
3) If separate invoices: which invoice recipient and remit-to address per entity?

I'll draft a short playbook for the ElanWare call (steps, owner, expected outputs). If we need legal approval for cross-entity revenue recognition, allow for an extra 48h.

-Karthik
Senior Finance Manager
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@elan-ware.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Sana Patel <sana.patel@elan-ware.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Split billing across ELW-US and ELW-EU for Q4 invoice

Hi Liam / Sana —

Thanks for the mapping file, that helped. For context: the Q4 invoice includes (1) usage charges for API calls, (2) professional services amortized from the onboarding SOW, and (3) a one-time premium support credit we applied in Oct. We need to map lines to entities as follows:

- Usage (API) -> ELW-US (60%) / ELW-EU (40%)
- SOW amortization -> ELW-US (100%) per SOW signature (contract is with ELW-US)
- Support credit -> allocate to the entity that owns the subscription (ELW-US)

Action items for ElanWare on the call: provide cost_center_code for each business unit so Karthik's team can populate the allocation matrix. If your ERP cannot accept line-level tags, we will produce two invoices.

Proposed call: Wed Dec 2, 10:00 PT — 30 min. Agenda: allocation matrix, remit addresses, VAT subtotal expectations.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

If Redwood can add a custom remittance block per entity on page 2 that lists the remit-to and cost center mapping, that will satisfy our AP intake.

Sana Patel

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Subject: Finalized playbook: multi-entity invoice distribution + payment collection cadence

Hi all —

Attached is the one-page operational playbook and our populated allocation matrix: 2026Q4-allocation-matrix.xlsx. Summary of the agreed approach:

1) Invoice format: single consolidated PDF with line-level entity tags and an EU VAT subtotal section. We will include a second-page remittance block that shows separate remit-to details and cost-center mapping for ELW-US and ELW-EU. This meets ElanWare's AP intake requirements and keeps document count to one.
2) Generation cadence: invoices will be generated on Dec 12 (final usage run) and issued Dec 13.
3) Collections / credits: AR will route payment reminders by entity; credit memos tied to SOW amortization will be issued to ELW-US only.
4) Ownership:
   - Redwood finance (karthik_iyer) — final invoice generation and tax/VAT subtotals
   - Redwood revenue ops (stephanie_nguyen) — playbook owner and communications
   - AE (marissa_cole) — any contract/discount clarifications and SOW confirmations

Attachments: 2026Q4-allocation-matrix.xlsx, Playbook-MultiEntity-Invoice-Redwood-OnePager.pdf, SOW-ElanWare-Redwood-2026.pdf

Please reply with any final concerns by EOD Dec 9. If no flags, we will schedule the generation and send the invoice Dec 13.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
